criteria_results.title: ISSUE_001: Identifies overbroad MAE carve-outs for environmental industry/regulations
criteria_results.reasoning: The memorandum expressly identifies the environmental-services-industry and Environmental Laws MAE carve-outs as problematic because they lack disproportionate-impact qualifiers, and it proposes adding those qualifiers to both carve-outs.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_001: Proposes adding disproportionate impact qualifier to MAE carve-outs
criteria_results.reasoning: The memorandum expressly proposes replacing both the environmental-services-industry carve-out and the Environmental Laws/regulatory carve-out with language excepting changes that disproportionately affect the Company relative to other industry participants.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_001: Provides actual revised contract language for MAE definition
criteria_results.reasoning: The memorandum provides actual replacement contract language for clauses (ii) and (iii) of the MAE definition, expressly adding exceptions where industry or Environmental Law changes disproportionately affect the Company relative to other industry participants.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_001: Explains rationale — environmental company needs MAE protection
criteria_results.reasoning: The memorandum specifically explains that Cascadia’s value is directly tied to environmental regulation and environmental-services demand, so absolute carve-outs for industry conditions and Environmental Law changes would remove the most relevant sector-specific risks from the MAE protection. This satisfies the required rationale.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_002: Identifies missing interim covenant restricting affiliate transactions
criteria_results.reasoning: The memorandum expressly identifies that Section 6.01(b) lacks a specific interim restriction on affiliate transactions and proposes a new covenant prohibiting the Company from entering into, amending, renewing, or terminating transactions with Seller or Seller affiliates without Buyer consent, subject to specified exceptions.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_002: Proposes covenant requiring Buyer consent for affiliate transactions
criteria_results.reasoning: Section 6.1 proposes new Section 6.01(b)(xiv), which prohibits the Company from entering into, amending, modifying, extending, renewing, or terminating transactions or agreements with Seller or its affiliates unless approved in advance in writing by Buyer, subject to specified exceptions.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_002: References the above-market rent to Seller affiliate as rationale
criteria_results.reasoning: In Section 6.1, the memorandum supports the interim affiliate-transaction restriction by stating that the Affiliate Lease costs $1,600,000 annually and noting its treatment as a related-party Adjusted EBITDA item. This connects the affiliate lease/rent arrangement directly to the covenant rationale.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_003: Identifies indemnification cap discrepancy (20% vs. 12.5%)
criteria_results.reasoning: The memorandum expressly identifies that the Seller's draft uses a 20% cap of $43,000,000, while the binding term sheet requires a 12.5% cap of $26,875,000, and proposes conforming revisions.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_003: Proposes redline reducing cap to 12.5% / $26,875,000
criteria_results.reasoning: The memorandum expressly proposes replacing the $43,000,000 / 20% indemnification cap with $26,875,000, equal to 12.5% of the $215,000,000 Base Enterprise Value, in both the definition and operative indemnification provision.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_003: References the term sheet as basis for cap correction
criteria_results.reasoning: The memorandum expressly cites the executed September 10, 2025 Term Sheet § 8 as the source fixing the general indemnification cap at 12.5% of the $215 million Base Enterprise Value ($26.875 million), both in the cap definition markup and the operative indemnification provision.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_004: Identifies that environmental reps survival period is too short
criteria_results.reasoning: The memorandum expressly identifies that Seller’s Section 9.01(b) applies a 12-month survival period to environmental representations, calls that period inadequate, and proposes extending Environmental Representations, including Section 4.15 Environmental Matters, to 36 months.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_004: Proposes extending environmental reps survival to at least 36 months
criteria_results.reasoning: The memorandum expressly proposes that the Environmental Representations survive for 36 months after closing and also reserves the option to seek survival for the full applicable statute-of-limitations period.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_004: References CERCLA/Dalton Creek exposure as rationale for longer survival
criteria_results.reasoning: The memorandum expressly connects the longer environmental-representation survival period to Dalton Creek CERCLA and active remediation risks. In Section 8.1, it recommends 36-month survival and explains that the DD memo shows “CERCLA and active remediation risks can mature years after Closing.” It also identifies Dalton Creek as a known CERCLA exposure with a 72-month special indemnity and discusses the ongoing Hargrove remediation.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_005: Identifies anti-sandbagging provision in Section 9.06
criteria_results.reasoning: The memorandum expressly identifies Section 9.06 as an anti-sandbagging provision and quotes its language barring Buyer from indemnification for breaches or inaccuracies of which Buyer or its representatives had Knowledge as of the Closing Date.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_005: Proposes replacing with pro-sandbagging language
criteria_results.reasoning: Section 8.6 expressly deletes the anti-sandbagging provision and replaces it with a pro-sandbagging clause stating that Buyer's indemnification and other remedies are not affected, limited, diminished, or impaired by any investigation or knowledge acquired before or after execution or Closing.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_005: Provides actual pro-sandbagging contract text
criteria_results.reasoning: The memorandum provides actual proposed pro-sandbagging contract language in Section 8.6, titled “Effect of Investigation and Knowledge,” stating that Buyer’s indemnification and other remedies are not affected by investigation, knowledge, notice, or other information.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_006: Identifies need for Special Indemnity for Dalton Creek CERCLA matter
criteria_results.reasoning: The memorandum expressly proposes a separate Dalton Creek CERCLA Special Indemnity in new Section 9.09, outside the general indemnification framework, with separate survival, basket, cap, escrow, and recovery terms.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_006: Special Indemnity survival of 72 months
criteria_results.reasoning: The memorandum expressly provides in proposed Section 9.09(b) that the Dalton Creek Special Indemnity survives until 72 months after the Closing Date, with timely asserted claims surviving until final resolution.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_006: Special Indemnity not subject to basket or cap
criteria_results.reasoning: The memorandum expressly states in proposed Section 9.09(c) that the Dalton Creek Special Indemnity is not subject to the Deductible, Basket Amount, Indemnification Cap, or other limitations applicable to general representation claims, and provides for first-dollar recovery outside the general cap.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_006: References Dalton Creek liability range ($1.5M-$6M)
criteria_results.reasoning: The memorandum expressly states that the Dalton Creek matter has estimated exposure of $1,500,000–$6,000,000, including in the deal facts and proposed Schedule 9.09 supporting the Special Indemnity.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_007: Identifies problematic earnout operational covenant
criteria_results.reasoning: The memorandum expressly identifies Section 2.05(d) as overly restrictive, quotes the requirement to operate consistently with past practice and in good faith to maximize the Earnout Payment, and recommends replacing it with a narrower primary-purpose covenant preserving Buyer's operational flexibility.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_007: Proposes limiting earnout covenant to no-frustration standard
criteria_results.reasoning: The memorandum expressly deletes the affirmative past-practice and earnout-maximization obligations and replaces them with a covenant prohibiting actions taken with the primary purpose of reducing or avoiding the earnout payment, while preserving Buyer's operational discretion.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_007: Explains rationale — Buyer integration/restructuring flexibility
criteria_results.reasoning: The memorandum expressly explains that the Seller’s broad earnout covenant would restrict Buyer’s post-closing integration, restructuring, personnel, capital allocation, pricing, and strategic decisions, creating litigation risk over ordinary business judgment. It also proposes language preserving Buyer’s discretion to integrate, restructure, and otherwise manage the Company.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_008: Identifies missing payoff letter requirement
criteria_results.reasoning: The memorandum expressly identifies that Section 2.03(d) permits repayment “at or promptly following the Closing” and notes that the draft does not require payoff letters before Closing. It also proposes delivery of executed payoff letters at least three Business Days prior to Closing.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_008: Proposes payoff letters at least 3 business days pre-closing
criteria_results.reasoning: Section 4.3 requires executed payoff letters no later than three Business Days before Closing, including wire instructions and commitments to provide lien-release documentation such as UCC-3 termination statements and other release instruments.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_008: Proposes simultaneous repayment at closing through funds flow
criteria_results.reasoning: The memorandum expressly replaces the 'at or promptly following Closing' language with a requirement that all Closing Indebtedness be repaid, discharged, and satisfied in full simultaneously through the closing funds flow at Closing. It also adds a corresponding closing condition.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_008: Proposes payoff letter delivery as a condition to closing
criteria_results.reasoning: The memorandum expressly proposes adding Section 7.02(h) as a condition to Buyer's obligations, requiring Buyer to receive the payoff letters at least three Business Days before closing and requiring the closing funds flow to provide for simultaneous repayment and discharge of all closing indebtedness.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_009: Identifies missing government contract anti-assignment/novation requirement
criteria_results.reasoning: The memorandum expressly identifies that the Seller's draft lacks specific government-contract anti-assignment, novation, and recognition provisions. It discusses FAR Part 42.12 and the Anti-Assignment Act, names the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers and Bureau of Land Management contracts, and proposes targeted representations, covenants, closing conditions, and post-closing cooperation.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_009: References specific government contracts requiring novation
criteria_results.reasoning: The memorandum specifically identifies two active federal government contracts requiring novation or recognition under FAR 42.12: U.S. Army Corps of Engineers Contract No. W912DR-21-D-0045 and Bureau of Land Management Contract No. L23PX-00412.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_009: Proposes closing condition or covenant for government contract novation
criteria_results.reasoning: The memorandum expressly proposes new Section 6.12 requiring Seller and the Company to prepare and submit federal novation or recognition requests under FAR Part 42.12 and to seek required government approvals. It also adds a Section 7.02 closing condition requiring all pre-closing novation, recognition, and change-of-control submissions to have been made, with no denial or threatened termination.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_009: References Anti-Assignment Act or FAR provisions
criteria_results.reasoning: The memorandum expressly cites both FAR Part 42, Subpart 42.12 and the Anti-Assignment Act as the legal basis for government-contract novation/recognition requirements, including in Sections 5.1 and 6.2.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_010: Identifies missing environmental permit transfer/notification covenant
criteria_results.reasoning: The memorandum expressly identifies that the Seller draft lacks a covenant addressing environmental-permit change-of-control notifications, approvals, transfers, or post-closing cooperation. It also proposes a new Section 6.13 requiring a permit matrix, pre-closing notifications and applications, efforts to obtain approvals, and post-closing cooperation for transfers, re-issuances, amendments, and related actions.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_010: Proposes cooperation covenant for environmental permit transfers
criteria_results.reasoning: The memorandum proposes new Section 6.13 requiring Seller to assist before closing with environmental permit notifications, applications, transfers, reissuances, amendments, and approvals, and to provide post-closing cooperation for at least 12 months or as reasonably necessary to complete those processes.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_010: Notes that permits may require notification even in a stock deal
criteria_results.reasoning: The memorandum expressly states that “A stock purchase does not eliminate change-of-control requirements” and explains that environmental permits across Oregon, Washington, California, and Nevada may require notice, consent, approval, transfer, reissuance, or amendment upon the ownership change.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_011: Identifies missing R&W Insurance subrogation waiver
criteria_results.reasoning: The memorandum expressly states in Section 8.7 that the Seller draft contains no R&W insurance subrogation waiver and does not address any R&W policy, then proposes a waiver of insurer subrogation rights against Seller except for actual fraud.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_011: Proposes subrogation waiver provision with fraud exception
criteria_results.reasoning: The memorandum proposes new Section 9.10 requiring the R&W insurer to waive subrogation, contribution, recourse, and other claims against Seller and related parties, expressly excepting actual fraud by Seller. It also identifies Granite Ridge Underwriters as the carrier in the accompanying commentary.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_011: References R&W Insurance policy / Granite Ridge Underwriters
criteria_results.reasoning: The memorandum expressly references Buyer obtaining an R&W insurance policy, identifies Granite Ridge Underwriters as the carrier, and connects the policy to a required insurer subrogation waiver against Seller except for actual fraud.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_012: Identifies non-compete scope exceeds term sheet (duration)
criteria_results.reasoning: The memorandum expressly identifies that the Seller draft imposes a five-year non-compete while the binding term sheet provides for three years, and it proposes replacing the duration with a three-year period.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_012: Identifies non-compete scope exceeds term sheet (geographic)
criteria_results.reasoning: The memorandum expressly identifies the geographic discrepancy in Section 9.1, noting that the Seller draft applies “anywhere in the United States” while the binding term sheet limits the covenant to four states, and the replacement language specifies Oregon, Washington, California, and Nevada.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_012: Identifies non-compete scope exceeds term sheet (activity)
criteria_results.reasoning: The memorandum expressly identifies that the Seller draft applies to “all U.S. businesses,” while the binding term sheet limits the restricted activity to environmental remediation and hazardous waste management services. It also provides replacement language conforming the covenant to that narrower scope.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_012: Proposes narrowing non-compete duration to 3 years
criteria_results.reasoning: The memorandum expressly replaces the seller draft's five-year non-compete with a three-year period in proposed Section 6.09(a), matching the term sheet.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_012: Proposes narrowing non-compete geographic scope to OR, WA, CA, NV
criteria_results.reasoning: The proposed replacement for Section 6.09(a) expressly limits the non-compete geographic scope to Oregon, Washington, California, and Nevada, matching the term sheet.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_012: Proposes narrowing non-compete activity scope to environmental remediation and hazardous waste management
criteria_results.reasoning: The proposed replacement for Section 6.09(a) expressly narrows the restricted activity to businesses engaged in “environmental remediation services or hazardous waste management services,” matching the term sheet’s specified scope.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_012: Notes enforceability risk of overbroad non-compete
criteria_results.reasoning: The memorandum expressly notes that the nationwide, all-business non-compete is materially overbroad, includes carve-outs to avoid restricting Seller's legitimate construction and timber operations, and states that the covenant should be reviewed for enforceability under applicable state law.

criteria_results.title: Indemnification cap issue rated as Critical or High priority
criteria_results.reasoning: The output expressly assigns the indemnification cap discrepancy (20%/$43 million versus 12.5%/$26.875 million) a Critical priority in Sections 3.2 and 8.2 and in the consolidated priority list.

criteria_results.title: Anti-sandbagging issue rated as Critical or High priority
criteria_results.reasoning: Section 9.06 is expressly labeled “Priority: Critical,” and the consolidated priority list also categorizes deletion of the anti-sandbagging provision and addition of pro-sandbagging language as Critical.

criteria_results.title: Memorandum identifies provisions acceptable as drafted
criteria_results.reasoning: The memorandum includes a dedicated Section 11, “Items not to mark up,” identifying multiple provisions acceptable as drafted and briefly explaining why, including the basket, knowledge qualifier, good-standing certificates, Delaware governing law, escrow amount, and Fundamental Representation survival.

criteria_results.title: Memorandum flags items for partner/client discussion
criteria_results.reasoning: The memorandum expressly flags issues for further partner/client discussion, including whether to require completed government-contract novation as a closing condition (to be escalated to Elena and Marcus) and whether to seek full statute-of-limitations survival for environmental representations after client discussion.

criteria_results.title: Escrow amount correctly stated as $16,125,000 (7.5% of EV)
criteria_results.reasoning: The memorandum repeatedly and correctly states the escrow amount as $16,125,000, equal to 7.5% of the $215,000,000 Base Enterprise Value, including in the deal facts, escrow release discussion, and items not to mark up.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_006: Proposes 36-month escrow holdback for Special Indemnity
criteria_results.reasoning: The memorandum expressly proposes a 36-month escrow holdback for Dalton Creek Special Indemnity claims, distinct from the 18-month general escrow release, including in Sections 8.4 and 8.5 and the closing recommendation.

criteria_results.title: Earnout maximum correctly referenced as $25,000,000
criteria_results.reasoning: The memorandum expressly states in Section 4.2 that the earnout's maximum is $25,000,000 and identifies that amount as correct.

criteria_results.title: Earnout Adjusted EBITDA threshold correctly referenced as $38,000,000
criteria_results.reasoning: The memorandum expressly states in Section 4.2 that the earnout's full-payment Adjusted EBITDA threshold is $38,000,000 and identifies it as correct.

criteria_results.title: Earnout floor correctly referenced as $32,000,000
criteria_results.reasoning: The memorandum expressly states that the earnout has a $32,000,000 floor and uses linear interpolation between that floor and the $38,000,000 full-payment threshold, satisfying the pro-rata requirement.

criteria_results.title: References playbook as authority for at least 3 markup positions
criteria_results.reasoning: The memorandum cites the Buyer M&A Playbook as authority for well over three distinct markup positions, including the MAE disproportionate-impact qualifier (Playbook § 2.1), indemnification cap ( §§ 5.1 and 14), earnout covenant ( § 7.2), payoff mechanics ( § 13.1(f)), government-contract provisions ( § 12.2), environmental survival ( §§ 4.1–4.2), pro-sandbagging ( § 5.3), and other provisions.

criteria_results.title: References term sheet as authority for at least 3 markup positions
criteria_results.reasoning: The memorandum cites the executed term sheet as authority for numerous distinct markup positions, including the indemnification cap, earnout covenant and mechanics, debt payoff procedures, survival periods, Dalton Creek Special Indemnity, escrow treatment, R&W insurance subrogation waiver, and non-compete restrictions. This exceeds the required three issues.

criteria_results.title: References environmental DD memo for at least one markup position
criteria_results.reasoning: The memorandum repeatedly cites the Environmental DD Memo as support for markup positions, including the Dalton Creek special indemnity, government-contract novation provisions, permit-transfer covenants, and environmental representation survival.

criteria_results.title: Memorandum identifies specific SPA section numbers for issues
criteria_results.reasoning: The memorandum ties well over 8 planted issues to specific SPA sections, including Sections 1.01 (MAE and cap), 2.05 (earnout), 2.03 and 2.08 (payoff mechanics), 4.15 and 4.16 (environmental and government-contract representations), 6.01 (affiliate transactions), 6.05/6.12 (government-contract covenants), 6.09 (non-compete), and 9.01, 9.04, 9.06, 9.08, and 9.09 (survival, cap, sandbagging, escrow, and special indemnity).

criteria_results.title: Proposed redline language is actual contract text for at least 8 issues
criteria_results.reasoning: The memorandum provides insertion-ready proposed contract text for well over 8 issues, including MAE qualifiers, the indemnification cap, earnout covenants and mechanics, debt payoff mechanics, government-contract representations and covenants, permit provisions, survival periods, the Dalton Creek special indemnity, pro-sandbagging, the R&W insurance waiver, and non-compete provisions.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_008: Identifies all three sources of Target indebtedness
criteria_results.reasoning: The payoff-letter provision expressly identifies all three sources of Target indebtedness: Cascade Mutual Bank's senior term loan, Pacific Lease Corp.'s equipment financing, and Evergreen Holdings Group, Inc.'s subordinated seller note. It also lists their respective principal balances of $28.0 million, $9.8 million, and $4.5 million.
